boundedEgressExceptions.purpose: Update-check: HTTPS GET /repos/DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp/releases/latest at startup for version detection
boundedEgressExceptions.note: Cannot be disabled by environment variable. Fires once per process startup. Response is discarded if network is unreachable. No source code, index data, or repository content is included in the request.

transport.networkNote: Stdio transport is loopback-only for all tool operations. The single bounded egress exception is documented above. No other external network access. Nomic-embed-code embeddings are bundled; no runtime model download.

scope.toolAllowlistNote: CBM_ALLOWED_TOOLS and CBM_ALLOWED_SUBOPERATIONS are Brain-admission documentation fields only. They are not read by the binary and do not restrict server-side tool dispatch. Brain-level access control is DOCUMENTATION-ONLY as of B8.4R: no client-layer enforcement has been proven or implemented. Write tools (index_repository, delete_project, manage_adr, ingest_traces) are approval-gated in this registry and require per-call Brain-operator confirmation, but this is an admission-policy constraint, not a runtime enforcement boundary.
scope.enforcementNote: No runtime enforcement of tool allowlist exists at either the CBM binary layer or the MCP client layer. The approval field on write tools is a Brain admission policy that must be enforced by the calling agent (Claude/Codex) honoring this registry before dispatching. If client-layer enforcement is implemented in a future task, update enforcementStatus to 'client-enforced' and cite the implementation evidence.

tools.name: index_repository
tools.note: Writes SQLite index to CBM_CACHE_DIR only; persistence=false (default) prevents repo-local writes

cache.autoWatchNote: auto_watch is a persistent per-cache config key (stored in _config.db). Set via: CBM_CACHE_DIR=<path> codebase-memory-mcp config set auto_watch false. The CBM_AUTO_WATCH env var is not read by the binary and has no effect. auto_watch=false prevents background re-indexing on file changes; the filesystem watcher thread still starts but takes no action.
